raised_by: lam_fix_f01_a1 (self-disclosed), corroborating an earlier self-disclosure by lam_cwo_04_a1
finding: lane isolation in this campaign is enforced by INSTRUCTION ONLY. Two agents in this book independently broke the exact-path law by listing shared directories, both disclosed it, and neither had any technical barrier preventing it. A third pattern is adjacent: agents can read any path under SP, so the blind-within-wave guarantee for the five review lanes rests entirely on each agent choosing not to look.
severity_assessment: no shipped impact in either instance: both were read-only, nothing was opened, and every claim in both deliverables was verified against the agent own orders and the staged inventories. The risk is not what happened; it is that the control that prevented harm was the agent goodwill rather than a boundary.
why_it_matters_here: the campaign buys its independence guarantees with blindness: dual-blind primaries, review lanes blind to each other, and a repair author who must not see another author output. Those guarantees are cited in close receipts as evidence. An instruction-only boundary makes them assertions about agent behaviour rather than facts about the system.
what_the_agent_recommended: filesystem-level enforcement rather than instruction-only, if lane isolation matters to the independence guarantees.
orchestrator_view: agreed in principle and outside this book close. Options range from per-agent scoped working copies (cheap, strong) to a read-broker (expensive). It is a campaign-architecture decision with cost, so it belongs to the controlling agent under OW-6 and possibly to the owner.
disposition: recorded, not actioned in this book. Raised for the Fable controlling agent at the next book boundary; the close receipt will state that blindness was instruction-enforced and that two self-disclosed listings occurred with no shipped impact.
